description: Compute a one-dimensional squared-Euclidean distance transform with the linear-time lower envelope of parabolas, returning both costs and lowest-index minimizing sites.

source.title: Distance Transforms of Sampled Functions
source.report: Cornell Computing and Information Science Technical Report TR2004-1963

output.encoding: interleaved [D[0],argmin[0],...,D[N-1],argmin[N-1]], where D[x]=min_i((x-i)^2+f[i]) and argmin[x] is the least index attaining the minimum

workspace.meaning: Two 128-entry signed 64-bit arrays hold envelope site indices and integer start coordinates (2,048 bytes); scalar loop state and bounded container overhead fit within the cap. Caller output is accounted separately.

contract.parabola: For each site i, define g_i(x)=(x-i)^2+f[i] over integer x in [0,N).
contract.envelope_order: Insert sites in ascending index order. For existing site p and new site q>p, compute first=floor((f[q]+q^2-f[p]-p^2)/(2*(q-p)))+1 using mathematical floor division. This is the first integer coordinate where q strictly improves p; equal-cost ties therefore stay with the lower site index.
contract.stack: Keep site indices and their first active integer coordinates in increasing order; pop the last site while a new first coordinate is <= its start, then append the new site. The first site uses a negative sentinel below all possible crossings.
contract.evaluation: Scan x from 0 through N-1, advance to the last envelope site whose start is <=x, and emit its parabola value and site index.
contract.bounds: The maximum output value is 1,000,000+127^2=1,016,129; crossing numerators have magnitude at most 1,016,129. All values fit signed 64-bit.
contract.complexity: The envelope inserts and removes each site at most once and the evaluation cursor advances at most N times: O(N) time and O(N) workspace.
contract.error_precedence: Validate the complete input frame before checking output nullness/capacity. Malformed input returns -1; otherwise null or undersized output returns -2 without writes.

references.primary: primary_oracle.py: construct the ordered lower envelope with exact integer first-improvement coordinates, then scan it.
references.independent: independent_oracle.py: evaluate every site at every integer coordinate and minimize the pair (cost,site_index).
